name: Dorsomedial approach to the navicular and cuneiform
corridor: Dorsomedial incision in the interval between tibialis anterior and extensor hallucis longus, protecting the anterior tibial neurovascular bundle, giving medial and lateral planes to the navicular, cuneiforms, and first two TMT joints

positioning.text: Position supine with the foot at the end of the table under tourniquet control.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark the tibialis anterior and extensor hallucis longus tendons and the navicular and cuneiforms.

incision.text: Center the incision over the fracture in the interval between tibialis anterior and extensor hallucis longus, raising a full-thickness flap without undermining.

superficial_interval.text: Protect the anterior tibial neurovascular bundle, and develop a medial plane for the navicular and medial cuneiform or a lateral plane for the 1st-2nd TMT joints and middle cuneiform.

deep_interval.text: Expose the target bones subperiosteally through the chosen plane, keeping soft-tissue stripping minimal to protect the navicular blood supply.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous tissue, the tibialis anterior and extensor hallucis longus tendons, the anterior tibial neurovascular bundle, and the navicular and cuneiforms.

structures_at_risk.text: The anterior tibial neurovascular bundle (dorsalis pedis and deep peroneal nerve) is the principal structure at risk.

danger_zones.text: The lateral edge of the interval near the anterior tibial neurovascular bundle is the danger zone.

retraction_hazards.text: Keep the flap full thickness without undermining and protect the anterior tibial bundle at the lateral border.

exposure.text: Exposes the navicular, medial and middle cuneiforms, and the first and second TMT joints and proximal metatarsals.

limitations.text: The anterior tibial neurovascular bundle limits lateral extension, and navicular blood supply must be preserved.

indications.text: Indicated for fractures of the navicular and cuneiforms and medial-column tarsometatarsal injuries.

closure.text: Close the wound in layers taking care to prevent skin tension.

complications.text: Complications include anterior tibial neurovascular injury, navicular osteonecrosis from over-stripping, and wound problems.

procedure_applications.condition: A medial column midfoot or tarsometatarsal injury needs dorsal access

questions.question: In which interval is the dorsomedial midfoot incision made?
questions.answer: Between the tibialis anterior and the extensor hallucis longus.

questions.question: Which neurovascular bundle is protected in this approach?
Why should the flap be full thickness with no undermining?
questions.answer: To preserve the skin blood supply over the dorsal midfoot.
